arguments.value: 28-year-old woman with primary Sjögren’s syndrome presented to prosthodontics seeking replacement of missing teeth and management of xerostomia, xerophthalmia, caries, erosions, and reduced vertical dimension. Clinical and radiographic examination showed one missing tooth (#36), remaining roots (#24, 27, 45), PFM crowns on #26, 31, 32, 41, and 42, periapical lesions at #16, 24, and 46, extensive restorations, and widespread caries and erosions. A full prosthodontic rehabilitation was planned, including extractions of #16, 24, 27, 38, and 48, endodontic treatment of multiple teeth, post-and-core restorations, a 2-mm increase in vertical dimension, PFM crowns and bridges, and a night guard, with oral hygiene measures and 3-month follow-up.
